newsitem.title: USA: House panel backs bill to ban large mackerel boats.
newsitem.headline: House panel backs bill to ban large mackerel boats.

text.p: The U.S. House Resources Committee approved a bill Wednesday to ban large fishing boats from harvesting mackerel and herring along the U.S. Atlantic Coast, a House aide said.

The bill, which passed with no opposition, would bar all vessels longer than 165 feet with horsepower of 3,000 or more, until the government assesses the fish stocks in the area and until regional councils allow big boats to return.
According to the National Marine Fisheries Serivce, stocks of mackerel and herring are healthy but could be threatened in the future if they are not carefully managed.

The panel closed a loophole in its original proposal before passing the bill to ensure that factory trawlers that had caught fish in the area years ago and wanted to return did not escape the ban, a committee aide said.
The bill, sponsored by New England lawmakers, now goes to the House floor.
Greenpeace marine campaigner Gerry Leape called the vote "very encouraging," but predicted that the legislation faced a tough road in the Senate.
